name: Roses over Monaco
description: Closing Idol or Icon (2021), 'Roses over Monaco' is That Boy Hi Hat at his most cinematic — a finale engineered to feel like one. The title alone sets the scene: luxury against the backdrop of the French Riviera at night, opulence as a survival story rather than a flex. Production leans widescreen, with layered synths and a slow-blooming arrangement that lets each section arrive like a scene change, and his flow follows suit — measured, unhurried, carrying the weight of late-night reflection. This is post trap rendered as triumph over adversity: the verses acknowledge the climb without dwelling in the wound, and the hook opens up into something genuinely uplifting. In the alternative rap lane, closers do the heaviest emotional lifting — they're the last word a listener carries — and That Boy Hi Hat treats the responsibility seriously. 'Roses over Monaco' doesn't just end the album; it reframes everything before it as prologue, the dark streets that made the roses necessary. It's one of the catalog's most composed performances: nothing hurried, nothing wasted. When the last note fades, the record has done what a great closer should — left you wanting to run the whole journey back.
